data.body:
CORRECTION TO THIS TICKET'S CERTIFIED PLAN — THE SHOWSTOPPER DOES NOT EXIST. Measured against the live production container, not read off the packaging.

THE CLAIM (plan Approach + ORDERING criterion (d) + comment 7's BLOCK finding): Dockerfile.reviewbot:83 omits --extra bedrock, therefore pydantic_ai.providers.bedrock is absent from the image, therefore bedrock_model.py:60-66 raises LLMConfigError on the first Bedrock call, therefore the class-slot flip alone would stop the LLM-Review gate voting on every landing.

THE MEASUREMENT. Container compose-review-bot-1 on i-00880b2c7f13527c5, image compose-review-bot:latest id 864df2fbfcaf, Created 2026-08-03T22:06:37Z — built from CURRENT main, which does NOT carry --extra bedrock:
  docker compose exec -T review-bot python -c 'from pydantic_ai.providers.bedrock import BedrockProvider; print("SYMBOL_OK", BedrockProvider)'
    -> SYMBOL_OK <class 'pydantic_ai.providers.bedrock.BedrockProvider'>
    -> exit 0 (captured directly, not through a pipe)
That is the exact import bedrock_model.py:61 performs. Installed in the image: pydantic-ai-slim 1.107.1, boto3 1.43.62, botocore 1.43.62.

WHY THE PREMISE IS WRONG. pydantic-ai-slim's bedrock extra contributes ONLY boto3 — this plan states as much ('pydantic-ai-slim 1.107.1's own bedrock extra resolves to boto3==1.43.62'). The pydantic_ai/providers/bedrock.py module ships in the BASE pydantic-ai-slim wheel; the extra gates that module's DEPENDENCY, not the module itself. boto3 is already installed independently via pyproject.toml's reviewbot extra ('reviewbot = ["fastapi", "uvicorn[standard]", "boto3"]') at exactly the version the bedrock extra would pin. So the image already satisfies the bedrock extra's entire content by a different route.

THE REASONING ERROR, named so it is not repeated: absence of the EXTRA was taken to imply absence of the MODULE, and the inference was confirmed by READING Dockerfile.reviewbot rather than by EXECUTING the import. The plan review that raised it, and my own verification of it ('Verified by me against the tree'), both read the same declaration. This is the epic's own recorded lesson in a new costume — the check shared the claim's assumption. Note the irony: the finding correctly identified that a boto3-based probe cannot prove the import resolves, then itself concluded the import fails without running it.

WHAT STANDS AND WHAT CHANGES.
* --extra bedrock IS STILL BEING ADDED, on a different and honest basis: the Bedrock provider's dependency is currently satisfied only INCIDENTALLY, by an extra that does not exist for that purpose. Remove boto3 from the reviewbot extra, or let pydantic-ai-slim's bedrock extra grow a dependency beyond boto3, and the provider import breaks at gate time in production. Declaring the extra makes it intentional and lock-enforced. This is the SAME fragility argument this plan already accepts when it rejects pointing REBAR_LLM_CONFIG_FILE at /app/.github/llm-providers/bedrock.toml because that file 'is present in the image only incidentally'.
* ORDERING criterion (d) is SATISFIED and its observation is recorded above — and it was satisfiable before any change, which is the opposite of what the criterion assumed.
* THE RISK FRAMING IS WRONG AND SHOULD NOT BE REPEATED: the cutover was never one flip away from taking the gate down. The safety-net-first ordering is still being honoured, but on its own merits (no cross-provider fallback by design), not because of an imminent packaging outage.

TWO FURTHER MEASUREMENTS FROM THE SAME PROBE.
* ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is present in the container, len=108, evaluated INSIDE the container. Confirms the 'retained by design' position. (An earlier read of mine reported UNSET; that was a shell-quoting artifact — the variable was expanded on the HOST, not in the container. Discarded.)
* The container sets AWS_DEFAULT_REGION=us-east-1 and REBAR_LLM_BEDROCK_REGION=us-east-1 and NO REBAR_LLM_FRONTIER_MODEL / STANDARD / TRIVIAL and NO REBAR_LLM_MODEL. So the bot runs on built-in class defaults resolving to anthropic:claude-*. THE PRE-CUTOVER ANTHROPIC BASELINE IS NOW EVIDENCED RATHER THAN ASSUMED.
